transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-04-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sarah Gomez (EchoSearch VP Product), Tom Lee (EchoSearch Staff Engineer), Priya Nair (EchoSearch Search Eng)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, demo of search relevance flow, discussion of latency/cost tradeoffs and security/compliance questions. Agreed to POC and to share pricing and benchmark plan.

00:00 Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the account, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. Quick round robin?
00:08 Sarah Gomez: Hi I'm Sarah, VP Product at EchoSearch, we're looking to improve our enterprise search relevance for our SaaS product.
00:12 Tom Lee: Tom here, staff eng, I'll be running the integration and benchmarks.
00:15 Priya Nair: Priya, search eng, focusing on ranking and signals.
:18 Maya: Great thanks. Quick agenda: we'll demo the hosted API embeddings endpoint, show how you can do vector search + rerank via Redwood's rerank endpoint, then cover perf, costs, and security. We'll leave time for Qs and next steps.
02:02 Liam Chen: Alright jumping into the console — bear with me, visual demo, I'm going to show a simple flow: we ingest docs, generate embeddings with our hosted embeddings endpoint, index them in your vector store or Redwood's managed vector index, and then at query time we do a coarse similarity lookup followed by our rerank endpoint which takes the top-K and does cross-encoder style reranking.
03:10 Tom: Quick Q, when you say "rerank endpoint" is that running a cross-attention model over concat of query+doc? How big are the models?
03:22 Liam: Yep, good question. The reranker is a sequence-level model that compares query and candidate text, it runs on Redwood-hosted models optimized for latency. We have small and medium rerank variants — small is around 0.2-0.4x latency of medium but lower accuracy, medium gives better MRR. We can show you perf numbers on a sample dataset.
04:05 Sarah: Are embeddings stored in Redwood or do you expect us to store them?
04:12 Maya: Both options. For hosted quickstarts we provide managed vector indices (optional), but many customers prefer exporting embeddings to their existing vector DBs (Pinecone, Milvus, your internal service). Rerank endpoint just needs the candidate text; you can pass top-K IDs and texts.
04:40 Priya: If we pass texts to rerank, does that increase cost a lot? We have long documents (average 800 tokens).
04:48 Liam: There's cost per token for the rerank step. We recommend chunking docs into passages to keep token counts bounded. Also Redwood supports prefix/KV caching for repeated queries so you can save on long-doc re-eval. For long docs we often do coarse retrieval over embeddings of 200-300 token chunks then rerank top 10.
05:30 Tom: Latency numbers? Our SLO is 200ms p95 for search interactions.
05:38 Liam: With hosted small reranker and a top-K of 5, typical p95 is ~120-200ms depending on sequence lengths and model. If you need stricter sub-100ms we recommend dedicated capacity or a smaller rerank model with warmed KV cache. We can run a benchmark against your sample workload to get actual numbers.
06:12 Sarah: Cost? Our CFO will push back if cost per query doubles.
06:18 Maya: Totally — cost/latency tradeoff is a big theme. Redwood Optimize gives batching suggestions and quantization profiles for lower unit cost. For hosted POC we can show cost estimates based on your query volume; many customers see a 2-3x improvement in cost by combining coarse embedding filtering + small reranker versus naive cross-encoder on full corpus.
07:01 Priya: Security — we have to be SOC2 and data residency conscious. If we use hosted, what data do you store?
07:10 Maya: By default, we retain logs and minimal telemetry for 30 days; customer data retention policies can be configured. We support enterprise controls: bring-your-own-key (KMS) for encryption, SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC, and detailed audit logs. For regulated data we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated. I'll attach the security pack.
08:05 Tom: Do you support VPC peering or private endpoints for hosted?
08:10 Liam: We offer VPC endpoints for certain regions and can do private connectivity for customers on dedicated plans. Hosted public API is TLS + auth, but for strict network isolation Dedicated/Private is the path.
08:30 Sarah: Demo part please — show a query flow with embeddings + rerank.
08:35 Liam: Sure, I'm going to run a live query against a 50k doc sample we loaded. First call: embeddings.create — returns vectors. Then we do a kNN search to get top 50, then call rerank with top 10 bodies.
09:05 [screen share — slack link to sample dataset shown]
09:20 Liam: hitting /v1/embeddings, response in 40ms for batch of 16. Then coarse search in vector DB returns candidates in 30ms. Rerank call with top 10 using medium reranker returns in 180ms p95 here.
10:00 Priya: There's some noise in transcription — sorry, that was my note. But the ordering and examples look OK. How do you pass metadata like recency boost?
10:12 Liam: You can pass signals in the rerank payload — we let you include numeric features (e.g., recency_score) and we combine them in the rerank scoring. There's also an API to apply a multiplier or post-filter. Some of the customers use a light-weight linear combiner before rerank.
11:00 Tom: For POC we'll need reproducible metrics. Can you export scoring traces?
11:06 Maya: Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-request latency, and per-route dashboards. We can give you a shared dashboard for the POC with the exact metrics (MRR, p95 latency, cost per query).
12:00 Sarah: Any gotchas with long tail queries or cold starts?
12:05 Liam: Cold starts can add ~50-80ms for an un-warmed model. That's where warm pools and KV cache help. For long-tail we recommend caching common prefixes and using approximate nearest neighbor configured for recall/latency tradeoffs.
13:00 Priya: We use an internal vector store and have 1M docs. Is there a limit for the hosted rerank?
13:08 Liam: Rerank operates on candidate lists — volume of your index doesn't directly impact rerank. For vector search, if you want Redwood to host indices, we support large indexes (100s of millions) but for high scale we often recommend dedicated capacity. For 1M doc POC hosted is fine.
14:20 Tom: Integration: how much engineering work?
14:25 Maya: Many teams integrate in a week for a POC — generate embeddings during ingestion and then modify query path to call search+kNN+rerank. We have SDKs and quickstart scripts. We'll share a sample script.
15:10 Sarah: Questions from legal — do you provide DPA and data processing terms?
15:15 Maya: Yes, we have DPA templates and can sign standard DPAs. I'll include the legal pack.
15:30 Priya: Replay of rerank endpoint — is it stateful (does it keep KV cache per session)?
15:36 Liam: The rerank call itself is stateless; the runtime uses per-customer KV cache for model states/KV to speed generation on streaming endpoints — more relevant for generation than rerank. But we do have caching for repeated long documents.
16:05 Tom: If the reranker is still too slow, could we host a small pipeline ourselves and use Redwood for embeddings?
16:12 Maya: Absolutely. You can mix and match: use Redwood hosted for embeddings and run your own lightweight reranker, or use Redwood's rerank for quality and fall back to your local model if latency spikes. Smart routing can do that automatically.
17:00 Sarah: Sounds promising. Let's talk POC scope — what do you need from us?
17:05 Maya: Sample queries + labeled relevance (gold) if you have it, expected throughput, and your success metrics (target MRR uplift, max p95 latency, cost target). We'll prepare a POC proposal and benchmark plan.
17:30 Sarah: We'll compile those and send by end of week.
17:45 Maya: Great. Quick recap of next steps: I'll send pricing/security/legal pack, Liam will draft benchmark plan and we schedule a deep technical session with Tom and Priya next week. Any other Qs?
18:05 Tom: One small ask — can you include an estimate for per-query cost for 1M queries/day in the pricing sheet?
18:12 Maya: We'll include a few scenarios (small rerank, medium rerank, dedicated).
18:30 Sarah: Thanks everyone, this is useful.
18:35 Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and the POC plan.
18:40 Meeting ends with action items and follow-ups.
